MINUTES
  Regular Meeting of the
  Gardena City Council
  Tuesday, December 14, 2021

In order to minimize the spread of the COVID 19 virus, Governor Newsom has signed
Assembly Bill 361. Please be advised that the Council Chambers are closed to the public and
that some, or all, of the Gardena City Council Members may attend this meeting
telephonically.

The Regular Meeting Notice and Agenda of the Gardena City Council of the City of
Gardena, California, was called to order via Zoom at 7:30 PM on Tuesday, December 14,
2021, Mayor Cerda presiding.

1.  ROLL CALL

  Present: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tem Rodney G. Tanaka; Council Member
  Mark E. Henderson; Council Member Art Kaskanian; and Council Member Paulette C.
  Francis; Other City Officials and Employees present: City Manager Clint Osorio; City
  Attorney Carmen Vasquez; and City Clerk Mina Semenza.

  At 7:07 p.m., the City Council recessed into Closed Session via Microsoft Teams, with
  the following in attendance: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tem Rodney G. Tanaka;
  Council Member Mark E. Henderson; Council Member Art Kaskanian; Council
  Member Paulette C. Francis. Other City Officials and Employees present: City
  Manager Clint Osorio; City Attorney Carmen Vasquez; Outside Counsel Lou Dumont;
  and Director of Administrative Services Ray Beeman and Transportation Director
  Ernie Crespo.

10. PLANNING & ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY COMMISSION ACTION SHEET

  10.A DECEMBER 7, 2021 MEETING
  The Planning Commission considered an Ordinance adopting changes to Title 17
  (Subdivisions) and Title 18 (Zoning) of the Gardena Municipal Code relating to the
  implementation of Senate Bill 9 allowing the subdivision of single-family
  residential lots into two and the creation of two residential units per lot as
  mandated by State law. The adoption of this Ordinance is not a project under
  CEQA pursuant to California Senate Bill 9. The Commission's consideration
  involved making a recommendation to the City Council.
  APPLICANT: City
  LOCATION: Citywide

  Commission Action: The Planning Commission voted 3-2 -0, approving
  Resolution No. PC 14-21, recommending that the City Council adopt Urgency
  Ordinance No. 1838 and Ordinance No. 1839.

  City Council: No action needed. This item is scheduled for the January 11,
  2022, meeting.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS – No Speakers

11. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES

  11.A City of Gardena Audit Reports for Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2021:
  Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR), Family Child Care and
  GTrans

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Ken Pun, President of The Pun Group gave a PowerPoint presentation.

  Council Member Henderson asked what the difference between CAFR and ACFR
  was. Kenneth Pun clarified that the name was changed because it is an offensive
  term in South Africa. Mayor Cerda thanked Kenneth Pun for the very informative
  report.

  This Item was Received and Filed

  5

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, seconded by Council
  Member Francis, and carried by the following roll call vote to Adopt
  Resolution No. 6541:

  Ayes:  Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, Council Members Francis, Henderson and

12. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS – COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT - No Items

13. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - ELECTED & CITY MANAGER'S OFFICES

  13.A Approval of the 2021 -2025 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the
  City of Gardena and the Gardena Management Employees Organization (GMEO)

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  City Manager Osorio presented a PowerPoint presentation. Administrative Services
  Director, Raymond Beeman and Director of Transportation Ernie Crespo, who were
  the primary negotiators, came into the meeting and were available for any
  questions.

  Mayor Cerda thanked City Manager Osorio for all the hard work that he and the
  entire team did throughout the negotiations.

  It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, seconded by Council Member
  Francis, and carried by the following roll call vote to Approve the MOU
  and authorize the City Manager to execute the MOU with a term of July 1,
  2021 through June 30, 2025:

  Ayes:  Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, Council Members Francis, Henderson and
  Kaskanian, and Mayor Cerda

  Noes:  None
  Absent: None

  13.B COVID-19 Update

  City Manager Osorio presented the update.

  6
   Mayor Cerda asked if the cases were separated by the Delta or Omicron variants.
  City Manager Osorio replied that it was not specified by variant and was a mixture of
  all variants of COVID cases.

14. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS – POLICE – No Items

15. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - PUBLIC WORKS - No Items

16. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - RECREATION & HUMAN SERVICES

  16.A Approve Memorandum of Understanding Between the South Bay Cities Council of
  Government (SBCCOG) and the City of Gardena Regarding Use of Allocated
  County of Los Angeles Innovation Grant Funds to Implement the City's Homeless
  Plan and Outreach Coordinator Program beginning January 1, 2022 through June
  30, 2023.

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Recreation and Human Services Director Stephany Santin presented a PowerPoint
  presentation.

  There was a lengthy discussion which included all members of the Council, City
  Manager Osorio, City Attorney Vasquez and Director of Recreation and Human
  Services Santin regarding the funding for the Homeless Plan and how it will be
  administered.

  It was moved by Council Member Francis, seconded by Council Member
  Henderson, and carried by the following roll call vote to Approve the MOU
  between the City of Gardena and South Bay Cities Council of Government
  to implement Innovation Grant Funds:

  Ayes:  Council Members Francis and Henderson, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka,
  Council Member Kaskanian, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  None
  Absent: None

17. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - TRANSPORTATION

  17.A Approve Contract with Commline, Inc. for purchase and installation of a Radio
  System for $433,488

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Council Member Henderson asked if we are not allowing competitive process to
  thrive if not associated with the JPA, and how would they have competed for this
  contract. City Manager Osorio said this is a sole source agreement simply because
  Commline, Inc. works directly with the INSB radio system network, which we are
  piggybacking off of, and that Commline, Inc. is the sole provider for the encryption
  that is in the radios. Council Member Henderson stated that he just wanted to make
  sure that as we move forward, and as more JPA’s get created, that Gardena is
  making sure everyone has an opportunity to compete for our business. Council

  7
   Member Francis asked if we were moving from a lease agreement to a purchase
  agreement and asked how long the contract was for. City Manager responded that
  it was a separate agreement with INSB. Council Member Francis asked about the
  maintenance, purchase and replacements of radios if lost. City Manager Osorio
  stated the maintenance and warranty only applies to the radio we have, if lost, we
  would replace it but if it gets damaged it’s under warranty and will be replaced.

  It was moved by Council Member Henderson, seconded by Council
  Member Francis, and carried by the following roll vote to Approve Contract:

  Ayes:  Council Members Henderson, Francis and Kaskanian. and Mayor
  Cerda
  Noes:  None
  Abstain: Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka
  Absent: None

18. COUNCIL ITEMS - No Items

19. COUNCIL DIRECTIVES - No Items

20. CITY MANAGER REMARKS RE: DIRECTIVES / COUNCIL ITEMS

  City Manager Osorio gave a verbal report of information to follow-up on matters that had
  been directed or requested by the Mayor and Members of Council. Those items were,
  as follows:

  1.  Gave a verbal update for Council Member Francis’ succession plan directive for
  the City of Gardena as it relates to the executive team, specifically City Manager
  and the Directors. He said should a department head go on a short-term leave,
  the department head has the discretion of designating an alternate for his/her
  position, if not, city manager can appointment internally. If long-term or a matter
  of separation from the position, the City Manager may select the interim director
  from an internal candidate pool or an external candidate pool by running a
  recruitment. Regarding City Manager, whether short or long-term, the City
  Council has discretion hiring a replacement from within for interim or permanent
  basis. If in absence of a qualified candidate internally, the City Council may elect
  to go on a national search for a recruitment of a City Manager. City Manager
  Osorio said he will provide a written memo.

  3. Invited Administrative Analyst Mary Simonell to present on Gardena Community
  Aquatic & Senior Center Prop 68 Grant Award. He thanked Mary Simonell for
  presenting and invited and thanked three Directors, Raymond Beeman, Allan

  4. He wished his kids a happy birthday for turning 10 years old on Saturday, and if
  they are still awake watching, to go to bed.

21. COUNCIL REMARKS

  1. COUNCIL MEMBER HENDERSON - He congratulated GTrans for their awards
  dinner and the Parks and Recreation for their holiday dinner. He also attended other
  meetings. He stated that since this is the last meeting of the year, he thinks that’s a
  great note “to go out on as a city” as we talk about success – our success is
  breeding more success as we continue to move forward and the success has to do
  with all of us, our community, our staff, all the employees that make us who we are.
  He reiterated what Councilwoman Francis stated, “this is just the beginning of new
  things to come”. He talked about the city having transparency being a responsive
  government, having high street quality in the state of California, lighting plans, tree
  plans, park plans now we’re working on a homeless plan, and getting through the
  worst part of a pandemic were tough decisions had to be made. He thanked his
  colleagues and everybody for always putting Gardena first and getting things done
  and for all the effort that they put in and making sure that we’re a top-notch
  community as Councilman Tanaka says “we are the jewel of the south bay” our next
  thing is to be the jewel of LA County and after that we’ll be the jewel of the State of
  California. He wished everyone a Happy Holidays and is looking forward to 2022.

  2. COUNCIL MEMBER FRANCIS - Since the last meeting, she attended a virtual
  conference with Assemblymember Al Muratsuchi; a Zoom meeting - Loss of State of

  9
   Homelessness Seminar; and attended the Winter Wonderland, where she seen the
  Jolly Trolley for the first time. She also attended the GTrans Award Banquet and
  thanked the GTrans team/staff for their dedication, good leadership and commitment.
  She also believed that municipal bus transportation should have been considered
  essential workers during this COVID time, since so many people depended on bus
  transportation. She also attended the CERT Training, the Search Teams Holiday
  Potluck, Breakfast with Santa, and the Jolly Trolley at Rowley and Freeman Park.
  She thanked the Recreation staff for a wonderful job. She has also attended the
  Citizens Redistricting Commission which is about to come to a conclusion and
  pointed out the City of Gardena is going to move out of congressional Maxine Waters
  43rd District into Ted Lieu 33rd congressional district and recommends that the city
  stays put. She stated that if anyone has a concern and wants to make a public
  comment, go to the website wedrawthelines.com. She also stated that as we close
  2021, she wants to encourage everyone to keep doing what they are doing and pray
  for everyone this Christmas year. She also thanked the Council
  Members/Colleagues for being passionate about our city. She is also looking forward
  to next year to create a greater vision for our city. She also stated not to be
  discouraged about the new variants and continue to wear your mask, practice social
  distancing, and keep sanitizing and we are going to get through this “better days are
  ahead”. She wished everyone a Happy Holidays and Merry Christmas.

3. MAYOR PRO TEM TANAKA – He stated that there’s standing committees that he
  attends all the time and believes that the important ones are the City events, like
  attending the Rotary Gobble, City Tree Lighting, Santa Claus showing off our new
  trolley and GTrans recognition, one driver in particular had a perfect driving record
  for 21 years with no accidents. He attended the Tri-City CERT, which was a great
  event. He went to see Santa Clause at Rowley Park and there were varies activities
  for all the kids. He expressed his appreciation and thanked all the city
  staff/employees for their dedication and hard work for everything that they do for the
  community, citizens, and children’s because “we do things that nobody else is
  doing”. He specially thanked the Recreation and Human Services Department. He
  hopes that next year will be twice as better, even with COVID. He wished everyone a
  Merry Christmas and Happy Holidays, and Happy New Year.

4. MAYOR CERDA – Since the last City Council meeting, she attended her monthly
  board meetings such as, the CCGA, Sanitation and the 2021 Conference of Mayors.
  She also attended the G3 Rosecrans Grand Opening. She participated in the
  Genesis Church food giveaway and then attended Wobble before you Gobble at
  Rowley Park and she thanked Parks and Recreation for working with the
  organization that put the event together. She also attended Al Muratsuchi
  Community Virtual Coffee Event, where she received great feedback from residents
  in the Gardena area, the COG Executive Legislative Meeting, the ADAAP Awards
  Ceremony, she was the keynote speaker for their Red Ribbon Awards Ceremony,
  she attended the Winter Wonderland and the Tree Lighting ceremony, she
  mentioned that she was able to get there early and it was great to see all the
  employees come together to make that event special, she gave a special “thank you”
  to all the departments involved; the tree lighting ceremony and then attended the
  GTrans award ceremony and congratulated them again on obtaining those two
  awards, she also attended Breakfast with Santa, the Parks & Rec holiday party, the
  Carnelian HOA holiday party, the Elks Build A Bear drive thru event, the employee

  10
   President, and the Winter Wonderland put on by Harbor Gateway. She congratulated
  our employees in getting the Prop 68 Grant award and was excited that we were
  able to purchase the Chase building so we can offer services on the northside of
  town. She thanked the entire City Council and all the employees we did not get to
  mention, we appreciate you, our residents appreciate you, we hear it back on our
  end from them, at the end of the day it is a team effort.

  5. COUNCIL MEMBER KASKANIAN - Since the last Council meeting, he attended all
  the events that were mentioned by his colleagues, he mentioned he would like to
  wish all of his Gardena family a Merry Christmas and Happy New Year, he hopes
  that everyone has a safe and healthy new year, he also congratulated GTrans on
  getting the two awards, he wasn't able to attend the celebration because he was out
  of the country, he then thanked his colleagues for working so hard to make Gardena
  a better place to live.
